note: Stage one, the gate on draft 2. Three verses. 9:4 and 9:8b, changed for his majors on draft 1, pass. 9:19 MAJOR taken (in finem → 'para sempre', decision in_finem). 9:10 'auxílio' for adjútor: minor on draft 1, MAJOR on draft 2 with the words unchanged — held (D24: the same thing happened three times at 118:114). 9:6 minor repeated, refused.

outcomes.remark: 'pelos séculos dos séculos' pluralises the singular → 'pelo século do século' (minor, second time)
outcomes.reason: As on draft 1: the glossary formula; the singular is not said in Portuguese prayer.

outcomes.remark: adjútor designates the one who helps; the translation puts the help given for the agent (MAJOR) → 'auxiliador'
outcomes.reason: Held against the gate on purpose. The glossary row adjútor → auxílio (open) was refused this same way at Ps 117:6–7 and held at 118:114 against a minor and two majors on unchanged words (D24: 'a repeated major is weighed, not obeyed'); the metonymy is the same as suscéptor → amparo (D19); the verse pairs it with refúgium → 'refúgio', a thing, which the Latinist passes. 'auxiliador' is long and rare. For the main session with the adjútor row.

outcomes.remark: in finem here expresses perpetuity; 'não perecerá até o fim' bounds the negation and can mean it will perish when the end comes (MAJOR) → 'não perecerá para sempre'
outcomes.reason: Right, and the blind reader of draft 1 had heard the same third reading. in finem → 'para sempre' in all three places (9:7a, 9:19 twice), with Matos Soares 1932; proposed for the glossary.

note: Stage one, draft 3 (revise_v3.py; draft 2 kept as prayed.v2.json): in finem → 'para sempre' in 9:7a and 9:19 (twice). 9:19 now reads 'Porque o esquecimento do pobre não será para sempre: * a paciência dos pobres não perecerá para sempre'.
